CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE M.NAGAPRASANNA  ORAL ORDER

The petitioners/accused 2, 3 and 4 are knocking at the doors of this Court calling in question proceedings in S.C.No.270 of 2020 and an order dated 08-08-2024 passed thereto whereby LXXI Additional City Civil & Sessions Judge, NC: 2024:KHC:50811 Bangalore City rejects the application of the petitioners seeking their discharge from the array of accused.

sentences.text: The 2nd respondent is the mother of the wife of accused No.1, who is now no more on her committing suicide.

A complaint comes to be registered on 04-03-2019 against these accused/petitioners along with accused No.1 by the mother of the deceased for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 354A(1), 304B and 34 of the IPC r/w Section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 ('the Act' for short).

The daughter of the complainant was married to accused No.1 and after two years of marriage, it appears,
the relationship between the members of the family of the accused, as also accused No.1 and the deceased turned horribly sore.
On 03-03-2019 the daughter of the complainant dies by committing suicide.
Therefore, offences were drawn in Crime No.92 of 2019, inquest was conducted and mahazar was drawn on the body.

From the NC: 2024:KHC:50811 investigation the offence under Section 304B of the IPC was not found and, therefore, the Police file a charge sheet in C.C.No.23816 of 2019 dropping the offence under Section 304B of the IPC and bringing in Section 306 of the IPC.
The matter was committed to the Court of Sessions and is presently registered as S.C.No.270 of 2020.
The petitioners file an application before the learned Sessions Judge seeking their discharge, which comes to be rejected by the impugned order.
It is this action that has driven the petitioners to this Court in the present petition.
4. The learned counsel appearing for the petitioners submits that all the allegations are against accused No.1 who is the husband of the deceased.
Thus, the petitioners have nothing to do with the suicide of the daughter of the complainant.
He would submit that these petitioners are simply drawn into the web of crime without any rhyme or reason.

5. Per contra, learned Additional State Public Prosecutor would vehemently refute the submissions to contend that these petitioners are also responsible in abetting suicide of the deceased and there are clear pointers towards the overt acts NC: 2024:KHC:50811 done by these petitioners as well.

Therefore, it is for the petitioners to come out clean in the full-blown trial.
6.
I have given my anxious consideration to the submissions made by the respective learned counsel and have perused the material on record.
7. The afore-narrated facts are not in dispute.
The relationship between the parties is a matter of record.

In the summary of the charge sheet, which is after evidence, the factum of how the petitioners are involved in the commission of overt acts is clearly indicated.

The 1st petitioner is said to have sexually harassed the daughter-in-law; the 2nd petitioner is said to have tortured the daughter of the complainant and the 3rd petitioner/accused No.4 has also the same leanings of overt acts committed by others.

Therefore,
- 10 - NC: 2024:KHC:50811 there are grave allegations and seriously disputed questions of fact to be considered.
8. What is necessary for an offence under Section 306 of the IPC, are ingredients of Section 107 of the IPC.

Section 107 of the IPC reads as follows:
"107. Abetment of a thing.--A person abets the doing of a thing, who-- First.--Instigates any person to do that thing; or Secondly.--Engages with one or more other person or persons in any conspiracy for the doing of that thing, if an act Sri Jagadish Raj Aras vs State Of Karnataka on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139977035/
6 or illegal omission takes place in pursuance of that conspiracy, and in order to the doing of that thing; or Thirdly.--Intentionally aids, by any act or illegal omission, the doing of that thing.
Explanation 1.--A person who, by wilful misrepresentation, or by wilful concealment of a material fact which he is bound to disclose, voluntarily causes or procures, or attempts to cause or procure, a thing to be done, is said to instigate the doing of that thing.

sentences.text: Illustration A, a public officer, is authorised by a warrant from a Court of Justice to apprehend Z.
B, knowing that fact and also that C is not Z, wilfully represents to A that C is Z, and thereby intentionally causes A to apprehend C.
Here B abets by instigation the apprehension of C.

Explanation 2.--Whoever, either prior to or at the time of the commission of an act, does anything in order to facilitate the commission of that act, and thereby facilitates the commission thereof, is said to aid the doing of that act."
All that is necessary under Section 107 of the IPC is, prima facie ingredients which are present in the case at hand.
Therefore, there is no warrant of interference at this stage of the proceedings.
It is for the petitioners to come out clean in a full-blown trial.
9. Finding no merit in the petition, the petition stands rejected.
Consequently, I.A.No.1 of 2024 also stands disposed.
